notes.title: Insight Into Sound Design for Mars Horizon & Mars Horizon 2
notes.content:
When you think of sounds in space, what do you think of? Is it the edge of your seat orchestral scores from Star Wars battles, the peaceful hums from the USS Enterprise, or perhaps it’s the sound of silence as planets rotate around the sun? 🪐 Whatever you think of, it’s something we thought a lot about in the original [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/765810/Mars_Horizon/]Mars Horizon[/url] and look to build on in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2281620/Mars_Horizon_2_The_Search_for_Life/]Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life[/url]. 

In this blog, we will be reflecting on the video game audio design of Mars Horizon, what we learned from that title, and what players can expect in terms of sound design from the sequel. This is also a great piece to learn more about video game audio design in general, if you’re wondering how to get a job in game sound design. We spoke to Auroch Digital’s Senior Audio Designer, [url=https://www.sebaudio.com/]Matt Walker (He/Him)[/url], as he has lead the game sound design on both Mars Horizon titles. 🎧

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43757573/408902c63aa5945e7521cf840e3f37c8e762e5a1.jpg[/img]
[h3]Our First Horizon – The Music of Mars Horizon 1[/h3]
With Mars Horizon being our first giant leap into a dedicated space-based title, we were discovering things for the very first time, as Matt explains with his approach to the games sound design:

[i]“In Mars Horizon, there wasn't huge scope to do much dynamically - much of the player’s time is spent within the Solar System as they look to branch their way through the ages and decades, advancing their pursuit of landing on Mars first.

“But to support this sense of progression as the player reaches a new era in space travel, they unlock a new layer to the vertically stacked music cues. This small system starts out very passive, almost independently a drone – but, by the time the player reaches the latter stages of the game, they'll [hopefully] not notice, but feel a greater sense of growth and layering as the supporting music cues are now awash with orchestral layers and textures that previously weren't there.”

“The Mars Horizon soundtrack is a digital orchestra, one that I believe is quite convincing. Many articulations can be worked and manipulated to suit a cue, but there's absolutely nothing wrong with taking advantage of the digital aspects of such a tool. 
  
 “One of the main takeaways from that development cycle are to never overlook UI (user interface) audio design - it's intrinsically vital to flow and player communication. The UI audio didn't see as much attention due to several factors, but it's an imbalance that won't be overlooked again.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43757573/68f5dc8cfda30621c491cb91c142bb47586ea672.png[/img]
[h3]The Process Behind Recording[/h3]
A game has so many audio cues, whether it be in the main menu, loading screen, or via the many interactions the player can make while playing the main part of the game. But what goes into creating these various sounds of a game? Matt shares some parts of his process for recording audio content for games:

[i]“The 'process' of producing sound effects (SFX), ambiences and music cues etc for games can differ greatly from one project to the next. My process often riffs on playing a build of the game [or portion of it] as early as possible, and then continually with each subsequent update. All this early experience helps to inform the live decision making I'll be doing when I get to my digital audio workstation to progress work. 

“Ultimately, any audio 'bed' in support of a screen or feature mustn't overstep its place in the mix, as the player will be making decisions and being communicated with via UI and other SFX. Ambiences will always have a skeleton of low, low-mid, mid, and high elements that make up the asset. These are mixed to suit any design behaviours that are to sit above it, without over-powering the player with unnecessary frequencies and additions.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43757573/78a0b5ce8bfe1fc0603ab558ba2a77df5818d683.png[/img]
[h3]Feeling Inspired to Go Beyond the Horizon[/h3]
With decades of sci-fi iconic sounds from video games and other forms of entertainment, what are some of the musical and sound influences behind Mars Horizon and for Matt Walker in general? As video game players, we all have our favourite soundtracks, but what are some of the scores that Matt looks to for inspiration? He says: 

[i]“For me, Mars Horizon's musical identity has always characterized the triumphs and risks undertaken by not only those in the cockpit, but more specifically those operating behind the curtain. It's about those skilled people and their families. 

 “With these ideas in mind, [url=https://open.spotify.com/track/03VwHCPypgqRiVKn15oaSx?si=972df20c07834f76&nd=1&dlsi=85a991c5fbe04f44]Kamen's 'Band of Brother's’ score[/url] and [url=https://open.spotify.com/track/1ykddd7K0DTA0yZizBbiQC?si=7af2b003b3e24698&nd=1&dlsi=fa938b2506684076]Chris Roe's suite of cues for 'Mission Control: Unsung Heroes of Apollo'[/url] were such huge influences. I listened to and studied those soundtracks relentlessly and fell head over heels for them both. [url=https://open.spotify.com/album/3VXWaBidEwDACYFANRVCEq?si=39Hzqm1kQzmRHHfKhOTwhg&nd=1&dlsi=b89ef362a6394dba]Giacchino's 'Medal of Honor: Frontline' soundtrack[/url] has long been a personal favourite of mine with the tone of that soundtrack being woven into the extended Mars Horizon soundtrack especially.

“As for all other SFX and general audio direction, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/464920/Surviving_Mars/]'Surviving Mars'[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/323190/Frostpunk/]'Frostpunk'[/url] were drawn from to capture their 'working/moving parts' tone - such tremendous game audio design, and very satisfying to interact with.  

“The Mars Horizon 2 audio design looks to build upon everything established in the previous game, but more specifically the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/289070/Sid_Meiers_Civilization_VI/]Civilization [/url]titles and even as far as the more recent [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/200510/XCOM_Enemy_Unknown/]XCOM [/url]games both offer lovely reference points from which to draw inspiration.” [/i]

_______________________________________________________

[previewyoutube=Iplxi6-uA64;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]The Sounds of Space - Mars Horizon 2 Ambience and Music Video[/h3]
To tie in with the Sounds of Space blog, we have also released a one-hour ambient music video to unwind to. The video features the entire Mars Horizon soundtrack, from Matt Walker himself, as well as alpha footage from the Solar System in Mars Horizon 2.

Witness the rotation periods of many planets across the galaxy alongside the varied and atmospheric soundtrack from 2020’s Mars Horizon. If you wish to own a copy of the soundtrack, it can be purchased on Steam.

The video has been assembled to help viewers relax, study, or escape their day-to-day lives and spend some time getting lost among the stars. Witness breath-taking views of various planets in our Solar System, as well as asteroid belts and moons.

Mars Horizon saw players landing on the red planet but, in Mars Horizon 2, you will be going even further and exploring various planetary surfaces in the search for life. We hope this video helps to create a peaceful backdrop for your daily activities and gives you peace of mind.
_______________________________________________________

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43757573/05ccec842ec2e7fdaec32534bcb6fd7a6f81edcb.png[/img]
[h3]What Players Can Expect in 2025[/h3]
With the news that Mars Horizon 2 will now release in 2025, players will have to wait a little longer before they explore the solar system and search for life. In the meantime, Matt has shared what players can anticipate from the game audio design:

[i]“Players can expect a natural extension from the original Mars Horizon. The intention was never to deviate far from what is great about the original - only build upon it and perhaps iron out creases following that original development cycle. I really feel Mars Horizon 2 offers a more robust and varied player experience with regards to audio design, all offering and adding to a gameplay loop that is fun with a sense of feeling. 

 “Mechanically, the game audio design is more granular than before and I've been a part of its implementation right from the start, whereas during the original Mars Horizon my contributions were evolving.”[/i]

A huge thanks to Matt for sharing his experiences of game audio design and giving us a preview of what to expect in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2281620/Mars_Horizon_2_The_Search_for_Life/]Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life[/url]. If you wish to pick up a copy of the original Mars Horizon, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/765810/Mars_Horizon/]it’s available on Steam[/url], while [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1457770/Mars_Horizon_Soundtrack/]the soundtrack for Mars Horizon is also available to purchase on Steam.
[/url]
We’ll have more news to share on what players can expect in 2025 in the new year. We can’t wait to share more information with you all. Keep watching the skies! ✨

notes.title: ICYMI: Mars Horizon 1 and 2 Panel – It’s Just Rocket Science
notes.content:
Hello Aurochnauts,     

Delayed in orbit? Rest assured, the latest transmission from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/tabletopfest]Digital Tabletop Fest 4: Roll of the Dice[/url] has arrived to keep you entertained! notes.content:
[h1]🔴Daring Expedition now live🔴[/h1]

[h3]Take new risks in Mars Horizon's Daring Expeditions update [b]LIVE NOW[/b]. Expect new dangerous missions, new flags, and plenty of Spacepedia updates. The Mars Horizon Daring Expeditions update is now live on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/a0d47c0059a07dafcf1d8453cfd0dc03ddfea33c.png[/img]

[h2]What's in Mars Horizon's Daring Expeditions update?[/h2]

[h3]New Mission: Space Tourist 🚀[/h3]
We've added a space tourist mission where you can elect to send a billionaire or an educator into space on their request. This is a high risk mission for your agency, possibly wrecking your reputation or granting you huge rewards. We've also added new narrative events and cinematics for this mission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/2c93e93f014e5a9869eb48d7a41ca6cc7e1c60a8.png[/img]
[h3]New Mission: Chinese Rover Zhurong 🌌[/h3]
This adds a new mission for players who are playing the Chinese space agency in the game; Chinese Rover Zhurong as a payload to send to Mars! We took inspiration from this recent dramatic accomplishment by the CNSA and have put it into our game along with brand new cinematics which reflect the activity of the mission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/39b4e67b455fc0bdb07375336c2e5f528ed21a88.png[/img]
[h3]New Mission: Philae / Rosetta Mission 🛰[/h3]
This adds a playable new mission where the comet that the Rosetta mission targeted appears in the Solar System - and you're able to research a mission to land on it just like ESA did. notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/8428e757211711f061739b41355b1216c1b6e057.png[/img][h1]Expanded Horizons is coming to PC and consoles on 22nd June 2021! [/h1]

Expanded Horizons is our huge free update for Mars Horizon. It's our biggest one ever and includes:
[list]
[*] [b]New Mission [/b]- Bringing you NASA's Perseverance Rover and the Ingenuity Helicopter which landed February 2021
[*] [b]Reusable Vehicles[/b] - Requested by you, we've added a reusable Wyvern Upper
[*] [b]Sandbox Mode[/b] - Heavily requested by the community the ultimate customisable Mars Horizon experience
[*][b] Iron Core Mode[/b] - Also community requested, the toughest way to play ever
[*] [b]Lots of gameplay improvements[/b] - UI improvements, a catch up mechanic and more, suggested by you
[*] [b]New Custom Agency logo[/b] - Send our cow to space
[*] The new Vehicle packs you've been enjoying are included for console too [/list]Plus:
[list]
[*][b]Nintendo Switch Demo[/b] - Try running your space agency on the go
[/list]
[b][url=https://www.aurochdigital.com/blog/2021/5/20/mars-horizon-free-update]Read our blog post to get full details about what's included.[/url][/b]

[h2]New Mission and Payloads: Mars Perseverance [/h2]
We’ve added a new mission which includes the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perseverance_(rover)]Perseverance Rover[/url] and the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingenuity_(helicopter)]Ingenuity Helicopter[/url], y’know, that mission that NASA recently sent to Mars? You can now play that mission yourself in Mars Horizon! 

New Spacepedia entries exist for this mission, you’ll be able to find out all about the Rover and helicopter as well as viewing their models at your leisure. Alongside this there are new narrative events  where important decisions will have to be made. And finally, There are new  cinematics for these payloads meaning you’ll get to see the little helicopter making its way across its new home!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/b52b49e00d0331fa0feb59e1d9eb7f1e5a480361.gif[/img]

[h2]Reusable Vehicles[/h2]
We’ve also added a reusable Wyvern Upper. This is an awesome addition to the game because we’ve been able to demonstrate some of the new reusable vehicle tech which is moving into the mainstream in real life space exploration. If you do well enough to unlock the Wyvern Upper, you’ll be able to re-use it which will save you both time and money! Keep an eye out for the brand new cinematic for this too, we’re really proud of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/e97d18336fcb4cc10bac849c54b6591d4b1a1429.gif[/img]

[h2]New game modes - Sandbox and Iron Core[/h2]
[h3]Sandbox Mode - The ultimate customisable Mars Horizon experience 👩‍🚀[/h3]
HIGHLY requested by the community, we’re now offering a Sandbox Mode for Mars Horizon players! You’ll be able to access Sandbox Mode from ‘Customise Experience’ in the main menu, meaning you really can experience Mars Horizon however you want.

What Sandbox Mode opens up for you:[list]
[*] Unlocks ALL upgrades
[*] Launches NEVER fail
[*] Unlimited mission gameplay battery
[*] FREE building moving
[*] Removing obstructions is FREE
[*] Starting funds 
[*] Starting support tier
[*] A save icon to identify these sandbox saves at a glance[/list]
[h3]Iron Core Mode - The toughest way to play Mars Horizon 💪[/h3]
We’ve added a new special game mode where you can’t cheat by save-scumming. Iron Core mode will save after EVERY SINGLE TURN whether you want it to or not. Like with Sandbox Mode, a save icon will identify these Iron Core saves to help differentiate it. This is the toughest way to play Mars Horizon to date, there’s no going back!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32764963/9fdcfa9a716d8c88538ebf24a814dcaffd192c21.png[/img]

[h2]New Custom Agency logo - Our lovely Aurochs! 🐮[/h2]
Recently we redesigned our studio logo, we absolutely love our new Aurochs. notes.title: Mars Horizon review - a modest leap for mankind
notes.content:
As my plucky yet oddly interchangeable astronaut plants the ESA's flag tall and proud on the moon's surface, I can't help but afford myself a smile. This is cool, and after a lot of hard work and a tense series of challenges to get my people to and from our celestial neighbour, I feel a real sense of achievement.

I'm also very aware of how hard it can be to capture the magic and wonder of space exploration. Mars Horizon, a turn-based management game about running a space programme and leading humanity to the stars, tries to strike a delicate balance between accessibility and visual splendour; and you can tell it's having to work to do justice to both.

When talking about developer Auroch Digital's own take on space exploration, it's impossible to ignore the elephant on the launch pad, Kerbal Space Program. The comparison is inevitable because there aren't many games that share their premise: space exploration, as defined by gritty hard science and engineering rather than the space fantasy of a Mass Effect.

notes.title: Kerbal Space Program 2 is far off, but Mars Horizon will take you to the stars today
notes.content:
Kerbal Space Program is a wonderful game about space and landing on the moon that is as inspiring as it is painfully inaccessible to people who don't understand how orbital mechanics work (so, everyone). It's the hero we need, but not the hero we deserve, and Mars Horizon is here to offer an alternative.

Released today, Mars Horizon is a game where you are in charge of a space agency at the dawn of humanity's journey into the stars. You need to research new vehicle parts to create more complex spacecraft, but you also need to research the missions these craft will be used on. There is also a more interactive base-building element, and you can research new building options to expand your space agency's facilities.

You'll be competing against other global agencies to achieve key milestones, such as the first EVA, first moon landing, and so on, with the ultimate goal of being the first agency to land a crewed mission on the surface of Mars. To get there, you'll have to make sure you're hitting enough research bonuses and generating enough revenue to get their first, although choosing to focus on tech as opposed to flashy missions is a legitimate way to go.

notes.title: Mars Horizon is basically Kerbal Space Program Tycoon, and it hits Steam in November
notes.content:
If you've got a major need for space games in the leadup to Kerbal Space Program 2, there's a solid alternative on the, er, horizon in the form of Mars Horizon. Rather than the simulation-first space exploration of Kerbal, Mars Horizon is about the day-to-day operations of a space agency in the style of the great tycoon games. And after numerous betas and demos, it's finally set to hit Steam in November.

Mars Horizon hits Steam on November 17, developer Auroch Digital has announced. The studio hasn't yet committed to a price, so no pre-orders either - but you can hit the Steam page to keep an eye out for further info on that front. You can also grab a demo there for an early look at what to expect from the game.

From the start of the space age through eventual Mars landings, Mars Horizon puts you in command of an agency trying to stay ahead in the competitive market of shooting metal death capsules through space. You can choose to emphasise the 'race' part of the space race, or slow things down to focus on more reasonable R&D.

Read the rest of the story...

We are looking for people to take part in an alpha weekend of our game and get your thoughts on how it is coming along and what else we can do to improve it?

The Alpha will start on [b]Friday 19th Jul[/b]y and finish on [b]Monday 22nd 2019[/b]. This also so happens to be the weekend of the 50th anniversary of the moon landings!

Interested?

[h1]How to get involved?[/h1]

Step 1: Sign up and [url=http://eepurl.com/gw5yUv]add your email address to our system[/url]
Step 2: Wait for your confirmation email
Step 3: Then, when the codes arrive we'll send you a Steam code 
Step 4: Log into Steam and redeem your code (there is a guide on how to do that here)
Step 5: Download and install Mars Horizon
Step 6: Launch rockets and send someone to space!
Step 7: Fill in the feedback form
Step 8: Get a free copy of the soundtrack when the game launches

On [b]Monday 22nd July at 10:00 (UK Time[/b]) the keys will expire. The feedback form will close on [b]Friday 26th July at 12:00 PM (UK Time)[/b].

So... what are you waiting for? Sign up now!

notes.title: We are working with the European Space Agency
notes.content:
Hi all,

We'll get straight too it: we are delighted to announce that we are working with the [url=http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Partnerships/Your_personal_space_race]European Space Agency[/url] on Mars Horizon!

We made the announcement [url=https://www.aurochdigital.com/blog/2019/3/4/esa-and-auroch]earlier today over on on our website[/url] and we are really excited to be working with such an important partner on making this game as authentic as we possibly can.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32764963/5b90293a69320c4c2d4243b58385dee10aebd20f.gif[/img]

Design Director, Tomas Rawlings, said "Working with ESA is a massive bonus for the Mars Horizon universe. Having access to real launch control specialists who can explain the real life pressures and challenges they face will help make this game as authentic as we can. With the upcoming ExoMars mission in 2020 this is a fantastic time for us to be working with the agency as they put the final stages of preparation on this launch. 

The involvement of the ESA is a double win for the gameplay as we’re not only getting to talk to people planning actual missions to Mars but also the people who plan the strategy of the agency itself - all of which we’re planning to use to help the gameplay. To say I’m excited by this partnership is an understatement, I’m (excuse the pun) over the Moon!"

notes.title: What is happening with Mars Horizon?
notes.content:
Hey there everyone!

We know we've been pretty quiet of late around Mars Horizon, but we wanted to give you a quick update of where we are, what is happening and why the radio silence.

[b]Release Date:[/b] We won’t lie to you. We don’t have one, yet. 

The main reason for this is actually really good news for the game. We previously mentioned before that we’ve had support from the guys at the UK Space Agency, but we also have been busy meeting with other [url=https://twitter.com/AurochDigital/status/1085869450136436738]space agencies like RALSpace[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/AurochDigital/status/1082584719789879296]talking with the European Space Agency (Esa).[/url]

I know this isn't the news many were hoping for, and we are sorry for that and the lack of updates, but we are sure these changes, and extra support from key space agencies, will be a big improvement on the game and well worth the wait!

But with that…

[b]Screenshots: [/b]

What better way to make it up to you than with some new screenshots? And boy howdy are these some beauties. These are an example of mission gameplay:

1. Static Failure Gif

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32764963/a614f2aeffb17ac365a5dd56df6d23e4c0f33cc4.gif[/img]

2. Camera Failure

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32764963/7617a716fa27f94cfae2e3d49b16b8558a6170ba.gif[/img] 

3. An awesome shot of Mars

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32764963/3ba9a2be5b8da20ed34355fdfd56ba15018ebc1b.gif[/img]

[b]What is next?:[/b] 

Well we wanted to give you an idea of what we're up to here, what the next stages are and what to expect from us.

The main thing is, [u]get the game done[/u]. Everyday it is getting closer and closer to being ready for wider sharing. 

We're also going to do a refresh of the Steam page and provide a more regular announcement update from around April time ([url=http://eepurl.com/dj1EY1]plus always worth signing up to our email newsletter![/url]).

[b]Any other news?[/b]

Well only one really cool one… [url=https://www.aurochdigital.com/mars-horizon-blast-off/]we've started a new Kickstarter called Mars Horizon: Blast Off![/url] - it’s a stand alone card game that came out of some gameplay prototypes we built for Mars Horizon - [url=https://www.aurochdigital.com/blog/2019/1/18/prototype-to-kickstarter]you can read the full story on our website.[/url]

[b]It launches on the 5th February[/b] and you can sign up to find out more by [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/profile/aurochdigitalltd/created]following us on Kickstarter[/url] or [url=http://eepurl.com/dPv2bz]signing up to the newsletter[/url].

We are also going to be doing a [url=https://twitter.com/AurochDigital]cosmic space fact session on Twitter soon[/url], so likes and RT are responded to with awesome space facts - don’t miss out!

Finally, if you do have any questions pop them in the discussion group and we’ll answer anything you throw at us!

Speak to you soon!

- AurochMatt and the team of Mars Horizon
